title: CONFIRMED GOOD: 3 transient Excel COM failures, 2 recovered by retry, 1 permanent - original kept and the UI reported the TRUE final count
detail: Full reconciliation of the only genuine conversion survivor in the matrix. O2 (log) records THREE Excel timeouts on m028: 'ekstraopgave 1 - VL.xlsx', 'HA.IT-reeksamen-2020-VL-Endelig1.xlsx' and 'OmkostningerAfsaetning - Ekstra - LOESNING.xlsx', each '[COM Timeout] Excel hung >180s ... Killing PID <n>' with a DIFFERENT pid, so the app spawned a fresh instance per attempt and reclaimed each hung one. O3 (disk) then shows exactly ONE surviving .xlsx and 60 PDFs - the other two converted on a later attempt in the same phase. O1 (completion screen) says '1 file could not be converted', i.e. the TRUE FINAL count, not the 3 transient errors, and explains it in the user's terms: 'The original file downloaded fine and is in your course folder - only the converted copy could not be made ... Close any open Office windows and run this course again to retry just it. Details are in download_errors.txt in each course folder.' Same screen also reports '24 files skipped because they exceeded the 5 MB limit'. So all three oracles agree at 1, the source-deleting converter kept the file it could not convert (the 2026-08-08 pdf_looks_real gate), and the user is told what happened and what to do. CORRECTS an earlier mid-run note of mine that said two originals were kept - that was a snapshot taken while the phase was still running; the end state is one.

title: HARNESS (recorded, deliberately NOT fixed mid-run): the log parser invents 3 of the 6 sync category labels, so O2 cannot corroborate them
detail: oracles/log.py PATTERNS['analysis_row'] matches (NEW|UPDATE-CLEAN|UPDATE-MODIFIED|DELETED-CANVAS|DELETED-LOCAL|IGNORED). sync/analysis.py:274-300 actually writes NEW, UPDATE-CLEAN, UPDATE-EDIT, CANVAS-DEL, LOCAL-DEL, IGNORED. So three labels never match and analysis_rows is permanently empty for locally-edited, deleted-on-Canvas and deleted-locally - including the category the RUNBOOK calls the most consequential in the suite, because getting edited files wrong is data loss. Confirmed on real evidence: s004's log parses UPDATE-CLEAN rows while s005's [UPDATE-EDIT] lines land in the parser's unmatched bucket, and the miss-rate monitor fired at 25%. SECOND layer: crosscheck._LOG_DETAILED_CATS restricts trust to {new, updated_clean} and justifies it with 'the other five appear in the Analysis complete counts and nowhere else ... Measured on a run whose analysis reported 2 deleted-on-Canvas and 2 ignored: the log contained zero rows for either'. That measurement is now STALE - the app was since changed to emit per-file rows for every category (its own comment says ignored files were 'previously counted nowhere and listed nowhere'). NOT a false-finding source today: with the regex broken, got_log is None and _categories_match correctly falls back to the review screen (O1), which is what the comment intends. NOT FIXED HERE ON PURPOSE: the selector is 'if want in _LOG_DETAILED_CATS or got_log', so repairing the regex would silently move those fixtures from O1 to O2 and can CREATE findings - a verdict-changing change, and 43 sync rows were mid-flight. The safe order (the RUNBOOK's own, from the ERROR-line narrowing) is: repair the regex, sweep both directions over the corpus comparing O1 vs O2 placement per fixture, then widen _LOG_DETAILED_CATS and refresh its comment in the same commit.

title: HARNESS (not a product defect): matrix collect appended instead of replacing, doubling every count in the report
detail: parallel.collect() opened the parent ledger with mode 'a' and deduped only WITHIN one invocation (the 'seen' set is local). The documented workflow invites running it twice - 'matrix collect' in the RUNBOOK setup section, then 'matrix recheck' + 'matrix collect --rechecked' in the re-check section - and the second call appended a full second copy. Measured on this sync run: 92 findings became 186, with all 92 keys duplicated exactly twice. It never changes a VERDICT (0 defects stayed 0) but it doubles every total the HTML report and the summary print, which is the number a reader trusts. The docstring's 'merges what recheck() re-derived INSTEAD of what the workers wrote' describes the SOURCE, not replacement of a prior merge, which is what made it easy to get wrong. FIXED: collect now rewrites the ledger, keeping findings that carry no 'lane' key. That split is the load-bearing part - lane findings are re-derivable, but a finding the agent recorded by hand is not, so a plain truncate-and-rewrite would silently destroy exactly the judgment findings the RUNBOOK asks for. Validated both directions on the real ledger: 186 -> 94, duplicated keys 92 -> 0, and both hand-added findings survived.
